defects.description: The rise from about 1 billion (1800) to more than 8 billion (today) is called 'a fourfold increase', but 8 divided by 1 is an eightfold increase.
paraphrases: 1 billion to 8 billion is eightfold, not fourfold.
The stated multiple understates the 1-to-8 increase.
Eight times one billion is an eightfold rise, not four.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'eightfold' (8/1). Findable from the two population figures, distinct.

defects.description: Growth is said to have 'more than doubled, falling to less than 1%' after peaking at over 2%, but a peak followed by a fall to under 1% is a decrease, not a doubling.
paraphrases: Falling from over 2% to under 1% is more than halving, not doubling.
'More than doubled' contradicts the rate falling to less than 1%.
The growth rate went down, so it cannot have doubled.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'more than halved' (2% to <1%). Findable from the peak and current rate in the same sentence, distinct.

defects.description: Today's 8 billion out of the ~108 billion who have ever lived is given as 'about 27%', but 8 / 108 is roughly 7%.
paraphrases: The share of people ever born who are alive today is overstated.
8 billion is roughly 7% of 108 billion, not 27%.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'about 7%' (8/108). Findable from the two figures in the same sentence, distinct.
